senses.definition: A partial covering for a floor.
(UK, Australia) A (usually thick) piece of fabric used for warmth (especially on a bed); a blanket.
examples:
1950 April, Dental Journal of Australia, Volume 22, page 181,
My own son had a bunny rug of which he was very fond and on being put to bed he would always demand his “bunny rug to suck his finger with.″

1958, Arthur Hailey, John Castle. Runway Zero-Eight. Bantham Books
She tucked in a rug round the woman. “How’s that?” The woman nodded gratefully.

quotes.text: They then cut down a quantity of gum-tree leaves for a bed, and threw their rugs upon them ready for bed-time.

quotes.text: Furnish every sleeping apartment with a sufficient number of toilet utensils and bedsteads, and sufficient bedding so that each bed shall be provided with a mattress, two sheets, a rug, and, in winter time, not less than one additional rug.
quotes.reference: 1906 July 27, Government Gazette of Western Australia, page 2297:

quotes.text: He brought with him a rug and a sheet, and lay down by the fire.

senses.definition: (historical, now rare) A kind of coarse, heavy frieze, formerly used for clothing.

quotes.text: They spin the choicest rug in Ireland. A friend of mine […] repaired to Paris Garden clad in one of these Waterford rugs.
quotes.reference: 1577, Raphaell Holinshed; Richarde Stanyhurst [i.e., Richard Stanihurst], “The Historie of Irelande […]”, in The Firste Volume of the Chronicles of England, Scotlande, and Irelande […], volume I, London: […] [Henry Bynneman] for Iohn Hunne, →OCLC:

senses.definition: (historical, now rare) A cloak or mantle made of such a frieze.
(obsolete, rare) A person wearing a rug.
A cloth covering for a horse.
(obsolete, rare) A dense layer of natural vegetation that precludes the growth of crops.
A rough, woolly, or shaggy dog.

quotes.text: The intervening years have been kind to Edward Fox and John Wells, who now assume the principal roles, in allowing them to keep their full complement of hair. Mr Fox shows his gratitude by using his rug as a prop, flopping it forward, Welsh-combing it back, letting it stand up on end as if from shock, while Mr Wells is content mostly to let his limply swathe his forehead.

senses.definition: (colloquial) A dense growth of chest hair.
(US, slang, ethnic slur) Ellipsis of rughead.
